paper_context.research_question: Can an attention-based deep neural network that combines BiLSTM (on dependency paths) and CNN (on lexical/auxiliary words)—together with automatic extraction of SIPs, sources, events and cues—improve event factuality identification on FactBank compared to rule-based and feature-based baselines?
contribution_style: modular pipeline (two-step: factor extraction + neural classifier)
main_claims: An attention-based neural framework that combines BiLSTM on shortest dependency paths and CNN on words (BiLSTM+CNN(Att)) yields better overall performance (micro- and macro-averaged F1) on event factuality identification on FactBank than several state-of-the-art baselines (rule-based Saurí, MaxEnt, CNN variants).
Using an attention-based CNN on pruned sentence structures improves detection of Source-Introducing Predicates (SIPs) over prior feature-based approaches.

A two-output design (one output for Uu/Non-Uu/other and a second for cue-governed modality/polarity among Non-Uu events) helps identify negative and speculative factuality values more accurately, addressing class imbalance.

Incorporating explicit inputs derived from syntactic structures—RS Path, SIP Path, Cue Path—and auxiliary words improves factuality prediction; SIP Path and auxiliary words are particularly beneficial.
expected_evaluation_dimensions: Classification performance per factuality category (CT+, CT-, PR+, PS+, Uu): precision, recall, F1
Aggregate performance: micro-averaged and macro-averaged F1 across categories
Ablation of input types (RS Path, SIP Path, Cue info, Auxiliary Words) to measure contribution of each input
Performance of basic factor-extraction components: event detection, SIP detection, source detection, cue detection (precision/recall/F1)
Comparison with prior baselines (rule-based, MaxEnt, CNN variants) on same dataset and splits
Robustness to class imbalance (especially low-frequency categories CT-, PR+, PS+)
Qualitative analysis / error analysis for common failure cases (e.g., embedded sources, complex syntax)

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The manuscript advances a two-step pipeline: (1) factor extraction (events, SIPs, sources, cues) using feature methods plus an attention-based CNN on a pruned-sentence (PSen) representation for SIPs; (2) a neural factuality classifier that encodes shortest dependency paths (SDPs) with BiLSTM (attention) and auxiliary words with CNN, producing two outputs (Uu/Non-Uu/other and cue-governed modality/polarity). Empirically, the BiLSTM+CNN(Att) model attains the highest reported micro- and macro-F1 on FactBank among the authors' baselines, with modest SIP detection gains and larger gains on rare negative/speculative labels (CT-, PR+, PS+). The paper argues attention, SDP-based BiLSTM, SIP path and auxiliary word inputs, and the two-output design are key to these gains. Several methodological and reporting gaps create uncertainty about whether gains stem from architecture, input representations, hyperparameter differences, or pipeline confounds (predicted vs gold factors). Statistical testing and ablation reporting are incomplete for rigorous chain-of-evidence verification.
logical_argument_graph: Node 1 (Motivation): Event factuality depends on syntactic factors (SIPs, cues, sources); accurate factuality helps downstream NLP.

Node 2 (Limitations of prior work): Rule- and feature-based systems rely on annotated factors or handcrafted rules and may not generalize; neural methods can learn representations from raw text and syntactic paths.
Node 3 (Pipeline proposal): Use a two-step pipeline—automatic factor extraction followed by neural factuality classifier—so the model can operate on raw texts.
Node 4 (SIP extraction innovation): Introduce PSen (pruned sentence) representation and an attention-based CNN to detect SIPs more reliably than prior feature-based methods.

Node 5 (Classifier architecture): Build BiLSTM over SDPs (RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path) + CNN over Auxiliary Words, with attention and two outputs (o1: Uu/Non-Uu/other, o2: cue-governed modality/polarity).
Node 6 (Rationale for two outputs): Separate decisions allow leveraging cue detection to improve minority-class (negative/speculative) identification and mitigate class imbalance.

Node 7 (Ablation logic): Compare variants (with/without attention, different input combinations, one-output vs two-output) to isolate contributions of attention, SIP_Path, Aux Words, and architecture choice (BiLSTM vs CNN).

Node 8 (Empirical claim): On FactBank 5-fold CV, BiLSTM+CNN(Att) outperforms Rules, MaxEnt, and CNN baselines on micro/macF1 and improves F1 for minority classes; attention and SIP_Path/Aux contributions supported by ablations.

Node 9 (Caveats): Factor-extraction errors, incomplete statistical reporting, limited per-ablation numerical detail, and potential implementation/hyperparameter confounds may weaken attribution of gains solely to the proposed model.

concerns.title: Unclear statistical testing and effect-size reporting
concerns.description: P-values are reported unevenly (e.g., p<0.05, p<0.001) without full specification of test inputs (per-fold metrics), effect sizes, confidence intervals, or multiple-comparison corrections. This weakens claims of significance across many pairwise comparisons.

Shared analysis: uncertainty flag noting small number of folds (n=5) and potential t-test assumption violations.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide per-fold micro/macro F1 scores for each model, report mean ± SD, compute effect sizes (Cohen's d), and apply a multiple-comparison correction (e.g., Bonferroni or Holm) when reporting many p-values; include test details in supplementary material.

concerns.title: Pipeline confound: predicted vs gold factor inputs
concerns.description: Downstream factuality classifier is trained and evaluated using predicted SIP/cue/source inputs from the extraction modules; the extent to which classifier gains depend on extraction quality is not isolated, risking misattribution of improvements to model architecture.
evidence: Section 5.1: baselines 'whose inputs are the outputs of our basic factor extraction for the fair comparison'; shared analysis notes assumption A1 about sufficiency of extraction outputs.
No reported 'oracle factor' experiments where neural model receives gold SIP/cue/source inputs.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run ablations where the classifier is fed (a) gold factor annotations, (b) predicted factors, and (c) mixed perturbations, to quantify sensitivity; report performance deltas to attribute improvements correctly.

concerns.title: Incomplete ablation reporting
concerns.description: Figure 6 and textual ablations claim SIP_Path and Aux Words are important, but numerical per-class P/R/F and variance across folds for each ablation are not provided, hindering reproducibility and verification.
evidence: Section 5.4 references Figure 6 and p<0.001 claim for SIP_Path effect, but lacks detailed tabular results.
Shared analysis: notes that numeric values and per-class breakdowns for each ablation are not fully tabulated.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Include a table (supplementary if needed) with per-ablation per-class P/R/F and per-fold scores, and report statistical comparisons between ablations.

concerns.description: Baselines and proposed models may not have been tuned or initialized equivalently (e.g., pre-trained embeddings, optimizer settings), which could bias comparisons.

concerns.actionable_suggestion: State precisely which embeddings and optimization/hyperparameters were used for each baseline, or re-run baselines under identical initialization and training regimes; if differences remain, add sensitivity analysis showing their impact.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: While combining SDPs with BiLSTM and attention is within trends of recent NLP research (not a radical novelty), the PSen representation applied to SIP detection and the specific two-output design for factuality classification are moderately novel engineering ideas; novelty alone doesn't guarantee validity—empirical robustness checks (oracle factor experiments, detailed ablations) are needed.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If factor-extraction modules (SIP/cue/source detectors) achieve substantially higher recall/precision (closer to gold), the classifier's architecture could reliably capture and leverage syntactic signals, validating the model design.
If per-fold variances are small and effect sizes remain large after proper statistical controls, observed improvements would more convincingly stem from architecture and attention mechanisms.
If ablations with gold factor inputs still show the BiLSTM+CNN(Att) advantage over baselines, this would disambiguate pipeline vs model contributions.
If attention visualizations consistently focus on linguistically interpretable tokens (SIPs, cues, auxiliary markers), the interpretability and causal claim strengthen.

novelty_lenses.rationale: BiLSTM over SDPs with attention and CNN encoding of lexical tokens follows well-established patterns in recent NLP work; the primary novelty is in input engineering and task-specific output structuring rather than a fundamentally new modeling paradigm.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes a two-stage pipeline: (1) factor-extraction (event detection, SIP detection via attention-CNN on Pruned Sentences, source resolution, cue detection) and (2) a two-output neural factuality classifier combining BiLSTM over shortest dependency paths (SDPs) and CNN over auxiliary words with attention. The core empirical claim is improved micro/macro F1 on FactBank vs rule-based (Saurí), MaxEnt, and CNN baselines. Evidence comprises basic extraction metrics (Table 3), per-class and aggregate F1 for classifiers (Table 4), ablations of input types (Figure 6), and some reported p-values from 5-fold cross-validation. Key assumptions include that predicted factor-extraction outputs are sufficiently accurate and comparable across systems, that SDPs and PSen preserve necessary information, and that the statistical testing is appropriate. Main methodological gaps: limited statistical details (per-fold scores, effect sizes, multiple-comparison correction), potential implementation/hyperparameter confounds between baselines and proposed model, limited isolation of pipeline vs model gains (no oracle vs predicted input experiments), incomplete numeric ablation breakdowns (per-class P/R/F for each ablation), and heuristic handling of multiple cues. Recommendations focus on reproducibility checks (provide splits, per-fold metrics, seeds, code), sensitivity analyses (oracle factor inputs, calibrated confidences, variations in parsing quality), and fuller reporting of ablation numbers and statistical tests.
logical_argument_graph: Premise P1: SIPs, sources, cues and syntactic paths are key determinants of event factuality (background + definition).
Premise P2: Pruned Sentence (PSen) preserves clause-level event structure and removes irrelevant tokens, permitting improved SIP detection via attention-CNN.
Premise P3: Shortest Dependency Paths (RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path) capture syntactic relations relevant to factuality; BiLSTM over SDPs plus attention can extract salient signals.
Premise P4: Auxiliary words (aux/mark dependents) provide additional pragmatic cues captured by a CNN.
Premise P5: Two-output design separates Uu/Non-Uu decision from cue-modality/polarity decision, helping class imbalance and cue-driven distinctions.
Method step M1: Build factor-extraction modules (event, SIP, source, cue) and use their predicted outputs as inputs for the main neural classifier.
Method step M2: Train models using 5-fold cross-validation with Word2Vec embeddings and SGD with momentum; report macro and micro F1.
Observation O1: Basic extraction achieves event F1=84.68, SIP F1=73.42, source F1=77.82, cue overall F1=66.04 (Table 3).
Observation O2: BiLSTM+CNN(Att) yields highest micro/macro F1 on All sources in Table 4 and improved minority-class F1s relative to baselines.
Conclusion C: The proposed attention-based BiLSTM+CNN with factor inputs improves event factuality identification on FactBank, and SIP Path + Aux Words and attention meaningfully contribute.

Caveat: This conclusion depends on (A1) extraction outputs being comparable and (A6) statistical tests being valid; if unmet, observed gains may reflect pipeline or evaluation artefacts rather than model superiority.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The manuscript advances event factuality identification by combining (1) an engineered factor-extraction pipeline (event, SIP, source, cue detection; PSen for SIPs) with (2) an attention-equipped neural classifier that fuses syntactic-path representations (SDPs encoded with BiLSTM+attention) and lexical/auxiliary encodings (CNN+attention). The system uses two outputs: one to separate Uu/Non-Uu/other and a second to assign cue-governed modality/polarity for Non-Uu events. Empirically, the authors report that this modular combination yields higher micro- and macro-averaged F1 on FactBank compared with a rule-based system (Saurí), a MaxEnt feature-based model, and CNN-only neural variants. Ablation experiments indicate SIP Path and Auxiliary Words materially contribute to gains; attention mechanisms improve over average pooling. The manuscript argues the principal novelty is (a) PSen + attention-CNN for SIP detection and (b) the particular BiLSTM-on-SDP + CNN-on-words architecture and two-output design tuned for factuality class imbalance. However, many components (SDP-based encodings, BiLSTM/CNN, attention mechanisms, two-stage pipelines) build on established techniques; thus the contribution reads as an informed combination and empirical evaluation rather than a fundamentally new paradigm. Key uncertainties concern whether performance gains stem from architectural innovations versus upstream factor-extraction quality, hyperparameter/implementation parity with baselines, and statistical-test rigor.
logical_argument_graph: L1: Event factuality depends on syntactic relations (SIPs, cues, sources) and lexical signals (aux words).
L2: Accurately extracting those factors from raw text enables using them as inputs (factor-extraction pipeline).
L3: Pruned Sentence (PSen) preserves SIP-relevant structure while removing noise => better SIP detection when encoded with attention-CNN.
L4: Shortest Dependency Paths (RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path) capture syntactic relations important for factuality => BiLSTM over SDPs yields effective path encodings.
L5: Auxiliary Words (aux/mark) carry pragmatic/syntactic cues => CNN encoding augments SDP features.
L6: Attention focuses representations on influential path tokens and pruned-sentence tokens, improving signal-to-noise vs average pooling.
L7: Two-output design decomposes Uu/Non-Uu decision from cue-mediated modality/polarity labeling => helps with class imbalance and minority-class accuracy.
L8: Combined system (factor extraction + BiLSTM+CNN(Att) + two-output) produces higher micro/macro F1 on FactBank vs selected baselines.
L9: Therefore, a modular pipeline that explicitly extracts factors and applies targeted neural encoders with attention yields empirically improved event factuality identification.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes a modular two-step pipeline for event factuality identification: (1) automatic factor extraction (event, SIP, source, cue) using feature-based classifiers and an attention-based CNN over a pruned-sentence (PSen) representation for SIPs; (2) an attention-equipped neural factuality classifier that combines BiLSTM over shortest dependency paths (SDPs) for syntactic-path features (RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path) and CNNs over auxiliary words, producing two outputs (o1: Uu/Non-Uu/other; o2: cue-governed modality/polarity among Non-Uu). The argument chain is: SIPs and syntactic-path signals drive factuality; an attention mechanism can focus on informative nodes in pruned structures and SDPs; a two-output design isolates cue-driven modality/polarity, helping with class imbalance; combined BiLSTM (for SDPs) + CNN (for auxiliary/lexical signals) with attention yields improved micro/macro F1 on FactBank versus rule-based, MaxEnt and CNN baselines. Empirical support includes basic factor extraction metrics (Table 3), main per-class and aggregate F1s (Table 4), ablations of input types (Figure 6), and p-values from 5-fold cross-validation t-tests. The authors claim statistically significant improvements for their BiLSTM+CNN(Att) model on several minority factuality categories and argue SIP_Path + Aux Words are primary contributors to gains. Key weaknesses in reporting and experimental control (detailed below) leave open alternative explanations (pipeline quality, implementation parity, statistical testing validity).
logical_argument_graph: Node A: Event factuality depends on sources, SIPs, cues, and syntactic relations (background premise).
Node B: Existing rule/feature methods rely on annotated factors and hand-crafted rules, limiting raw-text applicability.
Edge A->B: motivates automated factor extraction + learned representations from raw text.
Node C: A Pruned Sentence (PSen) preserves potential source tokens and clause-level event indicators while removing noise.
Node D: Attention-based CNN over PSen can detect SIPs more effectively than prior feature-based SIP detectors.
Edge C->D: PSen makes CNN efficient and focused; attention selects key tokens within PSen.
Node E: Shortest Dependency Paths (SDPs) connecting SIP/RS/cue to event capture essential syntactic relations for factuality.
Node F: BiLSTM over SDPs (with attention) captures bidirectional syntactic signals better than CNN on paths.
Edge E->F: choice of BiLSTM justified for sequence context.
Node G: Auxiliary words (aux/mark dependents) encode pragmatic/syntactic cues useful for factuality.
Node H: Two-output architecture separates Uu detection from cue-driven modality/polarity decisions, easing class imbalance.
Edge D,F,G,H -> I: concatenated learned representations + attention feed two-output softmaxes (o1,o2).
Node I: BiLSTM+CNN(Att) yields higher micro/macro F1 on FactBank compared to Rules, MaxEnt, and CNN baselines (empirical claim).
Edge I supported by: Table 3 (factor extraction) + Table 4 (per-class F1) + Figure 6 (ablations) + reported significance tests.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper presents a modular two-step pipeline for event factuality identification on FactBank: (1) a factor-extraction stage (event, SIP, source, cue detection) including a novel Pruned Sentence (PSen) representation and attention-based CNN for SIP detection, and (2) a neural factuality classifier combining BiLSTM (over shortest dependency paths: RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path with attention) and CNN (over auxiliary words) with a two-output design (o1: Uu/Non-Uu/other, o2: cue-governed modality/polarity). Empirically, the authors report higher micro- and macro-averaged F1 than several baselines (Rules, MaxEnt, CNN variants), modest SIP detection gains versus Chambers' features, improved minority-class (CT-, PR+, PS+) detection attributed to the two-output design and attention, and ablation evidence that SIP_Path and auxiliary words contribute materially. However, several methodological/reporting gaps introduce uncertainty: statistical testing details (t-test on 5-fold CV) are under-specified and multiple-comparison corrections are not reported; the pipeline uses predicted factor-extraction outputs without oracle-vs-predicted sensitivity experiments, leaving attribution of gains ambiguous; ablation and single-output vs two-output numeric breakdowns are presented mainly graphically or selectively; cue detection recall for PR is low (47.97%), risking downstream bias; heuristic multiple-cue resolution uses highest o2 confidence without calibration evidence. Below I reconstruct the claim-evidence links, flag uncertainties, list strengths and concrete concerns with actionable suggestions, offer alternative interpretations, and provide controlled novelty assessment under the creativity safeguards.
logical_argument_graph: A: Factuality requires modeling sources, SIPs and cues -> motivates factor-extraction stage (events, SIPs, sources, cues).
B: PSen prunes irrelevant tokens, preserving structures needed to detect SIPs -> attention-CNN on PSen yields SIP detection F1 73.42 (vs 72.56 using Chambers features).
C: Factuality decisions are driven by relations between event and linguistic factors -> encode SDPs (RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path).

D: BiLSTM over SDPs captures bidirectional syntactic context; CNN over auxiliary words captures non-path lexical cues; attention focuses on informative elements -> combined BiLSTM+CNN(Att) yields best micro/macro F1 on FactBank (Table 4).
E: Two-output design separates Uu/Non-Uu detection from cue-governed modality/polarity -> improves detection on rare negative/speculative classes (CT-, PR+, PS+).
F: Ablations show SIP_Path and Aux Words materially increase aggregate F1 (Figure 6) -> supports importance of explicit syntactic and auxiliary inputs.
G: Statistical significance claims (p-values) are reported on 5-fold CV results for some comparisons -> author claim of significance, but test assumptions/details unclear.

H: Pipeline confound: predicted factors feed into classifier and baselines use same extracted factors -> intended fairness, but extraction errors (e.g., PR cue recall) can distort downstream results if errors interact differently with architectures.

uncertainty_flags: Absolute improvement is small (~0.86 F1 points); no statistical test reported for SIP comparison.
Exact parity of the Chambers baseline setup (training data, features, preprocessing) is not fully detailed; differences could account for the small delta.

identified_claims.claim_text: A two-output design (one output for Uu/Non-Uu/other and a second for cue-governed modality/polarity among Non-Uu events) helps identify negative and speculative factuality values more accurately, addressing class imbalance.
evidence: Section 5.3: single-output variant reported worse F1s for CT-, PR+, PS+ (49.43, 33.06, 37.07) while two-output achieves (53.89, 41.83, 42.97) for BiLSTM+CNN(Att).
Authors argue two design reasons: cue assistance and imbalance handling.
uncertainty_flags: Numeric breakdown for single-output comparison is selectively reported; per-fold variance and statistical significance of the one-vs-two-output differences are not fully presented.
Interaction with cue detection errors (upstream) is not isolated — two-output gains may depend heavily on cue extractor quality.

identified_claims.claim_text: Incorporating explicit syntactic-path inputs (RS Path, SIP Path, Cue Path) and auxiliary words improves factuality prediction; SIP Path and auxiliary words are particularly beneficial.
evidence: Figure 6: ablation bars show lowest performance with RS_Path only; adding SIP_Path increases Micro/Macro F1 substantially; adding Aux Words gives further improvement.
Section 5.4 explicitly states 'SIP Path can greatly improve the results (p < 0.001)'; auxiliary words make further improvement.
uncertainty_flags: Figure 6 is plotted graphically without numeric per-class and per-fold values for each ablation combination; p-value reporting is summary-level without test details.
Potential co-linearity among inputs (e.g., SIP_Path and Cue_Path capturing overlapping info) not discussed.

identified_claims.claim_text: Using attention (in CNN for SIP detection and in BiLSTM/CNN for main model) improves performance over average pooling variants.
evidence: Table 4 compares Avg vs Att variants: e.g., CNN+CNN(Avg) vs CNN+CNN(Att) and BiLSTM+CNN(Avg) vs BiLSTM+CNN(Att); attention variants have higher aggregate scores.
Section 5.3 reports p < 0.001 for CNN+CNN and p < 0.05 for BiLSTM+CNN improvements after adding attention.
uncertainty_flags: Exact statistical test formulation, per-fold score distributions, and multiple-hypothesis considerations are not fully documented.
Category-specific gains vary; some categories show small or no improvement.

identified_claims.claim_text: The factor-extraction components achieve event detection F1=84.68, SIP detection F1=73.42, source detection F1=77.82, and cue detection overall F1=66.04 (with type breakdowns).
uncertainty_flags: Experimental setup for these extractions (cross-validation details, use of same splits, parser preprocessing) are described but not exhaustively; performance variability by fold not provided.
PR cue recall is relatively low (47.97%), which could limit downstream PR+ detection and bias results.

strengths.title: Linguistically grounded modular pipeline
strengths.description: The two-step pipeline cleanly separates factor extraction (events, SIPs, sources, cues) from neural classification, aligning system design with linguistic theory about sources and cues.
evidence: Sections 3 and 4: detailed descriptions of SIPs, sources, cues, PSen representation and the two-stage design.
Prior-stage summaries noting 'clear pipeline decomposition' and 'architectural alignment with task linguistics.'

strengths.title: Task-focused architecture combining SDPs and auxiliary lexical features
strengths.description: The model explicitly encodes shortest dependency paths with BiLSTM (attention) and auxiliary words via CNN, matching model components to hypothesized information sources for factuality.
evidence: Section 4.1: RS_Path, SIP_Path, Cue_Path definitions; Section 4.2: BiLSTM with attention; Section 4.3: CNN for Aux Words.
Ablation results in Section 5.4 showing SIP_Path and Aux Words improve performance.

strengths.title: Targeted handling of minority factuality classes
strengths.description: Designing a two-output architecture to separate Uu/Non-Uu decision from cue-driven modality/polarity addresses class imbalance and yields improved F1 on CT-, PR+, PS+ categories.
evidence: Section 5.3: reported per-category F1 improvements for BiLSTM+CNN(Att) with two-output design; single-output vs two-output comparison described.
Prior-stage reviewers highlighted empirical focus on minority classes as a strength.

strengths.title: Practical engineering of PSen for SIP detection
strengths.description: Pruned Sentence (PSen) is a concrete, computationally-light representation intended to preserve clause-level event presence while removing noise for SIP detection.
evidence: Section 3.2: PSen definition and examples (S4/S5), followed by attention-CNN applied to PSen.
Reported SIP F1 (73.42) slightly above Chambers' reimplemented baseline (72.56).

concerns.title: Attribution confound from predicted factor-extraction pipeline
concerns.description: The classifier is trained and tested using outputs of the (imperfect) factor-extraction stage. Without oracle-input experiments, it's unclear how much of the reported classifier improvement owes to model architecture versus pipeline differences or interactions with extraction errors.
evidence: Assumption A1 in shared analysis notes reliance on predicted SIP/source/cue outputs.
Cue detection PR recall is low (47.97) per Table 3, which could disproportionately affect PR+ downstream performance.
Prior-stage reviewers emphasize missing oracle vs predicted sensitivity experiments in evaluation_targets.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run controlled ablations where the downstream factuality classifier is given: (a) gold factor inputs; (b) predicted factor inputs (current setup); (c) mixed oracle/predicted (e.g., gold cues only). Report per-class metrics and per-fold variance for each condition to attribute gains precisely.

concerns.title: Statistical testing under-specified and potentially invalid
concerns.description: Reported p-values are based on two-sample two-tailed t-tests over 5-fold cross-validation, but per-fold metrics, independence assumptions, effect sizes, and multiple comparison corrections are not provided, undermining claims of statistical significance.
evidence: Section 5.1: 'divide corpus into 5 folds ... choose two-sample two-tailed t-test.'
Section 5.3: several p-values reported (p < 0.05, p < 0.001) without test details or effect sizes.
Shared analysis and prior reviewers flagged t-test over n=5 folds may violate independence and be underpowered.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide per-fold scores for each model (preferably for each class and aggregate), compute paired tests appropriate for cross-validation (e.g., paired t-test on per-fold differences or nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank), report effect sizes (Cohen's d), and correct for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg).

concerns.title: Incomplete ablation and numeric reporting
concerns.description: Ablation results (Figure 6) and some comparisons (single-output vs two-output) are presented graphically or selectively without full numeric per-class P/R/F, per-fold breakdowns, or significance tests, reducing reproducibility and interpretability.
evidence: Figure 6 is a bar plot without tabulated numeric values or per-class breakdowns per ablation.
Single-output vs two-output comparison lists a few numbers but lacks full per-class/per-fold stats.
Multiple reviewers requested full numeric tables in evaluation_targets and chaining_notes.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Release numeric tables for each ablation and model variant (per-class P/R/F, micro/macro, per-fold results), and run significance tests comparing key ablations (e.g., with/without SIP_Path, with/without Aux Words) showing confidence intervals.

concerns.title: Potential implementation/hyperparameter parity issues vs baselines
concerns.description: Although baselines are said to use the same extracted factors for fairness, details on hyperparameter tuning, embedding initialization, random seeds, and optimizer schedules for baselines vs proposed models are limited, so performance differences could partly reflect implementation choices.
evidence: Section 5.1 mentions Word2Vec initialization and SGD with momentum for authors' models, but not explicit hyperparameter tuning details for MaxEnt and CNN baselines beyond 'CNN+CNN variant'.
Prior-stage reviewers raised implementation parity as an open risk.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Document hyperparameter search procedures for baselines and proposed models, specify random seeds and initialization procedures, and (if possible) provide code or exact config files to ensure fair replication.

concerns.title: Heuristic multiple-cue resolution and classifier calibration
concerns.description: When multiple cues of different types exist, the system selects the cue with highest o2 confidence; no calibration or analysis of o2 score reliability is provided, risking systematic errors where confidences are miscalibrated.
evidence: Section 5.1: 'we adopt the cue with the highest confidence score in o2' for PR vs PS tie-breaking.
Shared analysis notes absence of confidence calibration analysis; cue classifier recall for PR is low (PR recall 47.97).
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Evaluate and report calibration of o2 confidences (e.g., reliability diagrams, expected calibration error), experiment with rule-based tie-breaking or ensembling cues, and report impact on downstream modality assignment.

concerns.title: Small absolute SIP detection gain lacking significance test
concerns.description: The SIP detection F1 improvement over Chambers' features is small (~0.86 points) and no statistical test is reported, so the claimed SIP detection benefit from PSen+attention-CNN may be within noise.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports SIP F1=73.42 vs Chambers features F1=72.56; authors note improvement is slight but argue SIPs are important.
No p-values or confidence intervals provided for SIP detection comparison.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report per-fold SIP detection scores and a statistical test (paired), or provide bootstrap confidence intervals to judge whether the SIP improvement is robust.

comparable_works.relevance: Primary rule-based baseline and dataset originator; provides earlier top-down dependency traversal approach and FactBank annotations used for evaluation.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Saurí's approach is rule-based top-down traversal; current work uses learned neural representations with extracted factors; evaluation on same dataset enables direct comparison.

comparable_works.relevance: Feature-based MaxEnt style prior work for factuality estimation used as a baseline.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Prior work used annotated predicate classes and pragmatic features; authors implement MaxEnt with a subset of features due to limited factor-extraction outputs.
comparable_works.source_trace: Section 5.1 describes MaxEnt baseline and feature availability caveats.

comparable_works.relevance: Feature-based event/SIP detection methods used as comparative baseline for SIP detection and event detection.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Chambers features are used for event and SIP detection; authors report improved event detection and slight SIP F1 gain using attention-CNN on PSen.

comparable_works.relevance: Use of shortest dependency paths and sequence models for relation and semantic tasks; conceptual precedents for SDP + LSTM encoding.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Authors adopt SDP encodings and BiLSTM with attention inspired by these works; novelty is combining SDP BiLSTMs with CNN on auxiliary words and two-output design focused on factuality.
comparable_works.source_trace: Section 1 and Related Work referencing these studies as motivators for syntactic-path encodings.

comparable_works.relevance: Cue detection lexical feature design referenced and reused for cue classification.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Authors use lexical features from Velldal et al. for cue detection, then pipeline them to neural classifier; cue detection performance (esp. PR recall) is a known weak point.

uncertainty_flags: Significance testing: reliance on t-test across n=5 folds without paired test details or multiple-comparison correction (Assumption A6).
Pipeline dependence: downstream evaluation uses predicted factor-extraction outputs (Assumption A1); no oracle experiments to disentangle effects.
Ablation reporting limited to plots without numeric per-fold and per-class tables (Assumption A3/A4).
Small absolute gains (e.g., SIP F1) may be within variance absent tests.
Cue detection PR recall low (47.97), risking biased downstream PR+ results; calibration of model confidences for multi-cue decisions not assessed (Assumption A8).
alternative_interpretations: Observed aggregate F1 gains might stem partly from optimized hyperparameters, embedding initialization or training regimen differences rather than architectural advantages if baselines were not equivalently tuned.

Performance improvements on minority classes could be amplified or diminished depending on cue-extractor errors; some apparent gains may reflect fortuitous interactions between extraction errors and classifier inductive biases rather than robust modeling of modality.

Small gains in SIP detection could be sampling noise; the downstream classifier might be primarily leveraging other inputs (e.g., auxiliary words or RS_Path) rather than improved SIP detection per se.

The attention mechanism may be acting in part as a regularizer or parameter reweighting beneficial for optimization rather than focusing on linguistically meaningful tokens; without attention weight inspection, it's unclear whether attention aligns with expected signals.
transparency_notes: The manuscript does not publish per-fold scores, random seeds, or code/config files; these would aid reproducibility and verification of statistical claims.
Ablation numeric tables, oracle-vs-predicted experiments, and calibration analyses for o2 confidences are not present but would materially strengthen causal claims.
Authors claim baselines use outputs of their factor-extraction stage for fairness, but details of baseline reimplementation and hyperparameter parity should be clarified or code released.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: Although components (SDP encodings, BiLSTM/CNN, attention, two-stage pipelines) each have precedent, the specific combination (PSen for SIPs, SDP-BiLSTM + CNN-Aux with two-output design) forms a task-oriented integration that can be novel in application. Novelty in combination does not guarantee methodological validity—empirical controls are needed to separate integration benefits from evaluation artifacts.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If factor-extraction components (SIP, source, cue detection) are near-oracle (high recall/precision), the classifier architecture will likely show clear improvements, validating the design.
If per-fold variance is low and attention consistently focuses on linguistically meaningful tokens, the gains are robust and replicable.

If baselines are re-run with identical embeddings and optimizer schedules and the proposed model still wins with statistically significant effect sizes after proper paired tests and multiple-comparison correction, the claim of architecture advantage holds.

novelty_lenses.verdict: Plausibly incremental novelty via informed combination
novelty_lenses.rationale: Individual modeling components (SDP encoding via LSTM, CNNs, attention) are established. The paper's contribution appears to be an informed integration tailored to factuality—PSen for SIP detection, SDPs for source/cue paths, Aux word CNN, and two-output architecture—yielding task-focused empirical gains.
evidence: Related Work cites Xu et al., Roth & Lapata, Chen et al. for inspiration; authors adapt these techniques to factuality.
Ablation indicates SIP_Path and Aux Words matter, suggesting the combination is purposeful.
uncertainty_flags: Degree of novelty depends on the robustness of empirical improvements and whether alternative simpler combinations were tested; small SIP gains and missing oracle experiments reduce certainty.

novelty_lenses.rationale: The approach does not introduce a fundamentally new modeling paradigm; rather it operationalizes known neural components with linguistically motivated inputs. It may be impactful within the factuality subfield but is unlikely to upend broader NLP paradigms.
evidence: Core elements (BiLSTM on paths, attention, CNN for words) have been used in relation classification and sentiment tasks; the paper applies them to factuality.
Performance gains are moderate and need stronger statistical backing.
uncertainty_flags: If the PSen idea shows consistent SIP detection improvements and enables new applications beyond FactBank, the contribution could be more influential than it appears.

confidence_interval.rationale: I am moderately confident (not certain) in the descriptive accuracy of the extracted claims and in the identified methodological concerns because claims are supported by tables and text in the manuscript. However, uncertainty remains about statistical robustness, attribution of gains (pipeline vs model), and reproducibility due to missing per-fold and oracle analyses; hence the interval is wide but skewed toward moderate-high confidence.

consensus_findings: The paper presents a clear, linguistically-motivated two-stage pipeline (automatic factor extraction: events, SIPs, sources, cues; then a neural factuality classifier) that is well-documented and modular.

The proposed BiLSTM+CNN(Att) architecture (BiLSTM on shortest dependency paths + CNN on auxiliary/lexical words, with attention) aligns with the task's linguistic intuitions and is evaluated thoroughly on FactBank with per-class and aggregate metrics.

Reported empirical results show BiLSTM+CNN(Att) attains the highest reported micro- and macro-averaged F1 among the compared systems in the manuscript, with particular gains on several low-frequency categories (CT-, PR+, PS+).
Attention mechanisms are reported to improve performance over average-pooling variants in both SIP detection and the main classifier.
Ablation claims indicate the SIP path input and auxiliary-word encoding materially contribute to aggregate performance, and the two-output design is linked to improved minority-class detection.
The authors provide explicit metrics for the factor-extraction components (event, SIP, source, cue), enabling diagnosis of upstream module quality.
disagreements: How novel the contribution is: some reviewers view the work as a useful engineering/combination of known neural components tailored to factuality (moderately novel), while others see it as largely incremental because core modeling primitives (SDP encodings, BiLSTM, CNN, attention) have clear precedents.

Whether the modest SIP-detection F1 gain (~0.86 F1 points vs Chambers' features) is practically meaningful: some treat it as a real improvement signal, others consider it possibly within noise unless statistical tests are shown.

Attribution of downstream gains: reviewers disagree on whether reported classifier improvements are primarily due to the proposed architecture (BiLSTM+CNN(Att) and attention) or whether they could be substantially driven by factor-extraction pipeline quality, hyperparameter/initialization differences, or other implementation choices.

Appropriate statistical methodology: reviewers uniformly urge more rigorous statistical reporting, but differ in emphasis on remedies (paired t-test vs nonparametric tests, bootstrap confidence intervals, multiple-comparison corrections).
uncertainty_hotspots: Statistical testing and reporting: p-values are reported without per-fold scores, effect sizes, confidence intervals, or corrections for multiple comparisons; 5-fold CV + two-sample t-test formulation may violate test assumptions.
Pipeline confound between factor-extraction quality and classifier architecture: no presented experiments where the classifier is fed gold (oracle) SIP/source/cue inputs to isolate model-level gains.
Ablation reporting gaps: Figure 6 and some one-output vs two-output comparisons are presented graphically or selectively; full numeric per-ablation, per-class, and per-fold P/R/F tables are missing.

Baseline and hyperparameter parity: insufficient explicit detail that baselines were trained/evaluated with identical embeddings, preprocessing, optimization, and tuning budgets; this raises risk of confounding implementation differences.

Cue-detection weaknesses and tie-breaking heuristics: PR cue recall is relatively low (≈48%), and multiple-cue resolution uses highest o2 confidence without calibration analysis—both can materially affect PR+/PS+ results.

Performance on complex/embedded-source sentences (low Uu F1 in embedded sources): limited qualitative error analysis to explain failure modes and to show whether architectural changes can address them.
model_diversity_effects: Pipeline modularity yields role-specific impacts: upstream factor-extraction errors (SIP/cue/source) propagate differently across classifier architectures; architectures that leverage SIP_Path and Aux Words more heavily will be more sensitive to extraction recall/precision than architectures relying on raw tokens.

Using predicted factor inputs for both baselines and proposed models reduces one form of unfairness but introduces entanglement: improvements may derive from how well each classifier exploits the particular extraction error patterns rather than from a universally better representation.

Attention vs average pooling variants show consistent but variable gains across categories; attention appears to benefit minority-class recognition and SIP detection, but the magnitude varies and may interact with input types (SIP_Path, Aux Words).

The two-output design changes the optimization landscape (decoupling Uu/Non-Uu and cue-driven modality), which can systematically favor better minority-class recall; this effect is architecture-level and dataset-distribution dependent.

Heuristic tie-breaking (highest o2 confidence) imposes an independence assumption on cues; models that produce better-calibrated confidences will be advantaged under this rule, creating sensitivity to calibration differences between model variants.
meta_review.editor_guidance: Treat the paper's empirical contributions and engineering of a modular pipeline as central, but require the authors to resolve the major methodological uncertainties before relying on the reported superiority as definitive. Specifically: (1) request experiments that isolate classifier-level contributions from pipeline effects (run the factuality classifier with gold factor inputs and with mixed oracle/predicted inputs); (2) demand full statistical transparency: per-fold micro/macro and per-class metrics, means ± SD, appropriate paired/nonparametric tests, effect sizes, and multiple-comparison corrections; (3) require complete numeric ablation tables (per-class P/R/F and per-fold scores) for all input combinations and one-output vs two-output variants; (4) require documentation proving baseline implementation parity (shared embeddings, optimizer settings, tuning budgets) or re-runs of baselines under matched configurations; (5) request attention visualizations and calibration analyses for o2 confidences and explicit evaluation on multi-cue sentences and embedded-source constructions. Preserve editorial centrality by asking for these targeted rebuttal/artefacts rather than making a binary accept/reject decision based on current materials.
meta_review.author_guidance: To strengthen causal attribution and reproducibility, provide the following in a revision or response: (A) Oracle-sensitivity experiments: run the downstream factuality classifier with gold (annotated) SIP/source/cue inputs, and with mixed-gold variants (e.g., gold cues only), and report per-class and aggregate metrics with per-fold breakdowns to quantify sensitivity to extraction errors. (B) Full statistical reporting: publish per-fold micro/macro and per-class P/R/F for every model variant and ablation, report means ± SD, effect sizes (Cohen's d), and use paired tests or bootstrap confidence intervals; apply and report multiple-comparison corrections. (C) Ablation tables: include numeric tables (supplementary if needed) for Figure 6 and for the one-output vs two-output comparison showing per-fold results and significance tests. (D) Baseline parity: explicitly state embedding sources, random seeds, optimizer/hyperparameter settings, tuning budgets, and any candidate filtering rules used for baselines; if current baselines are not matched, re-run them under identical training regimes. (E) Attention and calibration analyses: visualize representative attention weights, provide qualitative examples where attention benefits/fails, evaluate confidence calibration of o2 (reliability diagrams, ECE), and report performance on multi-cue sentences including alternative tie-breaking or learned aggregation. (F) Error analysis on embedded-source/complex syntax cases: provide examples and, if feasible, experiments with extended context encoders or alternative path windows. (G) Release code, data splits, random seeds, and scripts for PSen construction and factor-extraction to enable reproduction.
transparency_report: What is present: clear architectural descriptions (equations and diagrams), tables reporting factor-extraction P/R/F (Table 3), per-class and aggregate classification F1 for main models (Table 4), and a plotted ablation (Figure 6). Hyperparameter choices for the proposed models are described.

What is missing or under-detailed: per-fold metric distributions and exact numbers underlying plotted figures; effect sizes and confidence intervals for reported p-values; explicit multiple-comparison control; full ablation numeric tables and per-class per-fold P/R/F for each ablation condition; attention weight visualizations and confidence calibration analyses; code and exact configs for baselines and preprocessing (PSen construction, candidate filtering), and random seeds or model checkpoints.

Practical replication barriers: without per-fold scores, seeds, and code for PSen and the factor-extraction pipeline, reproducing the exact reported significance tests and attributing gains to architecture versus pipeline engineering will be difficult for independent researchers.
epistemic_limits: This synthesis is constrained to the manuscript text, tables, figures, and the specialist reviewers' analyses provided; I have not re-run experiments or inspected the code/data. Consequently I cannot verify numerical claims, reproduce p-values, or determine unreported implementation details (random seeds, exact embedding files, parser versions). Observed empirical improvements may change materially under re-run with different seeds, matched baseline hyperparameter tuning, alternate cross-validation splits, or when classifiers are fed oracle factor inputs. The reviewers' disagreement about novelty and attribution reflects these information gaps. Any judgment about the generalizability of the reported gains beyond FactBank (to other genres, languages, or different cue distributions) is inherently speculative without additional experiments.

human_facing_meta_review.summary: The manuscript proposes a modular two-stage system for event factuality on FactBank: an engineered factor-extraction pipeline (event, SIP, source, cue detection; PSen + attention-CNN for SIPs) followed by an attention-equipped neural factuality classifier that encodes shortest dependency paths with BiLSTM and auxiliary words with CNN, using a two-output design to separate Uu/Non-Uu and cue-driven modality/polarity. The authors report that BiLSTM+CNN(Att) achieves the highest micro- and macro-averaged F1 among their compared baselines (Tables 3 and 4), with particular gains on several low-frequency classes (CT-, PR+, PS+). Ablations indicate SIP Path and auxiliary-word inputs matter and attention improves over average pooling. However, important methodological and reporting gaps (statistical-testing details, lack of oracle-input sensitivity experiments, incomplete numeric ablations, and baseline/hyperparameter parity) leave ambiguity about causal attribution of improvements to the proposed architecture versus pipeline engineering or implementation choices.
strengths: Clear, linguistically motivated modular pipeline that separates factor extraction (events, SIPs, sources, cues) from learned factuality classification, enabling targeted component evaluation (Table 3).

Model architecture aligns modeling primitives with task signals: BiLSTM+attention on shortest dependency paths (RS/SIP/Cue Paths) and CNN for auxiliary words, which is conceptually appropriate for syntactic/lexical cues.

Empirical emphasis on rare but important factuality labels (CT-, PR+, PS+) and a two-output design intended to mitigate class imbalance, with reported per-class F1s showing improvements on these categories (Table 4).

Engineering contribution of Pruned Sentence (PSen) representation for SIP detection combined with attention-CNN is a concrete, task-focused idea with a documented (albeit small) SIP F1 gain (Table 3).
limitations: Attribution ambiguity due to pipeline confound: the factuality classifier is trained and evaluated using predicted factor-extraction outputs (SIP/source/cue). No experiments are reported where the classifier is fed gold (oracle) factors or mixed oracle/predicted inputs, so it is unclear how much classifier gains depend on extraction quality (shared_assumption A1; see Table 3 vs Table 4).

Statistical testing and reporting are under-specified: p-values are cited from 5-fold CV/t-tests without per-fold numeric scores, effect sizes, degrees of freedom, or corrections for multiple comparisons. Using two-sample t-tests over only 5 folds may violate test assumptions and inflate Type I error (see Section 5.1 and shared_analysis uncertainty flags).

Incomplete numerical ablation reporting: Figure 6 and some one-output vs two-output comparisons are presented graphically or selectively in prose without full per-ablation per-class P/R/F tables and per-fold breakdowns, hindering reproducibility and verification of claimed input contributions.

Potential baseline/hyperparameter parity issues: the manuscript provides hyperparameters for proposed models but does not fully document that baselines (Rules, MaxEnt, CNN variants) were trained/tuned under identical embedding initializations, optimizer schedules, and tuning budgets; differences could partially explain reported gains.
open_questions: Please provide oracle-sensitivity experiments: what are per-class and aggregate micro/macro F1 when the downstream factuality classifier receives gold SIPs, gold cues, and gold sources (individually and jointly)?

Please publish per-fold numeric results (per-class P/R/F and micro/macro) for all reported systems and ablation conditions, plus means ± SD, so statistical tests can be reproduced; specify whether reported t-tests were paired or unpaired and provide effect sizes and corrected p-values for multiple comparisons.

How were the baselines (MaxEnt, CNN variants, Rules) implemented and tuned relative to the proposed models? Provide exact embeddings used, random seeds, optimizer parameters, early-stopping criteria, and hyperparameter search budgets to verify implementation parity.

For sentences with multiple cues, how often does the highest-confidence o2 tie-breaker select the correct modality in held-out data? Provide calibration analysis (reliability diagrams or ECE) for o2 confidences and accuracy on multi-cue events under alternative aggregation strategies.

Can the authors provide attention visualizations and qualitative examples (successful and failed cases) showing what tokens or path positions the attention mechanism focuses on, and an error analysis for low Uu F1 on embedded sources?

What is the sensitivity of results to parsing quality and SDP extraction (e.g., use different dependency parsers or noisy parses) and to random seed variability (report robustness across multiple runs)?
consensus_snapshot: All reviewers agree the paper presents a well-motivated modular pipeline mapping linguistic factors (SIPs, sources, cues) to modeling components and that the BiLSTM+CNN(Att) design is appropriate for encoding syntactic paths and auxiliary words.
All agree reported empirical improvements on FactBank (Tables 3 and 4) appear plausible and that attention contributes positively versus average pooling.

All reviewers request stronger statistical reporting, oracle-input experiments to isolate pipeline effects, full numeric ablation tables, and evidence that baselines were trained under comparable conditions.
disagreement_snapshot: Degree of novelty: some reviewers view the contribution as a useful engineering/compositional novelty (PSen + two-output design), while others regard it as incremental since core modeling primitives (SDP-BiLSTM, CNN, attention) are established.
Practical importance of the SIP detection gain (~0.86 F1): some treat this as an innovation signal, others consider it possibly within noise absent significance testing.

Interpretation of minority-class gains: reviewers differ on whether two-output design and attention genuinely provide robust improvements across settings or whether those gains might be dataset- or pipeline-specific.
uncertainty_snapshot: Uncertainty about statistical robustness of reported p-values and effect sizes due to lack of per-fold data and multiple-comparison correction.
Uncertainty about causal attribution of classifier-level gains versus factor-extraction pipeline quality because oracle-input experiments are absent.
Uncertainty about generalizability beyond FactBank (other domains/genres) because failure modes (embedded sources, multi-clause sentences) are insufficiently analyzed.
source_trace: FactBank evaluations and per-class/aggregate F1 reported in manuscript Tables 3 and 4 (basic factor-extraction metrics and classifier per-class F1s).
Section 3.2 and Table 3: Pruned Sentence (PSen) design and SIP detection F1 = 73.42 compared to Chambers (2013) reimplementation (72.56).
Section 4 (architecture) and Section 5.3 (results): BiLSTM+CNN(Att) model description and text citing improvements on micro/macro F1 and minority-label F1s.

Section 5.1: experimental protocol note on 5-fold cross-validation and statement 'We choose two-sample two-tailed t-test for significance test' (shared_analysis A6 and reviewers' methodological critiques).
Section 5.4 and Figure 6: ablation claims that SIP_Path and Aux Words improve aggregate F1 (figure plotted; numeric values not fully tabulated).
transparency_notes: The manuscript includes clear architectural descriptions (equations, diagrams), reported P/R/F for factor-extraction modules (Table 3), and per-class and aggregate classifier F1s (Table 4). Missing or under-detailed items: per-fold numeric results underlying reported p-values (no means ± SD or effect sizes), full numeric ablation tables (per-class P/R/F per ablation and per-fold), explicit statement of whether t-tests were paired and degrees of freedom, multiple-comparison correction, precise baseline training/hyperparameter parity (embedding files, random seeds, optimizer settings), PSen construction scripts, and code/checkpoints. These gaps impede exact reproduction of statistical tests and causal attribution.
human_facing_meta_review.editor_guidance: Request that authors address the main methodological uncertainties before relying on the reported superiority as definitive. At minimum, require: (1) oracle-sensitivity experiments feeding gold SIP/source/cue inputs to the classifier and mixed oracle/predicted ablations; (2) full per-fold numeric results (per-class P/R/F and micro/macro) with means ± SD, effect sizes, and appropriately paired/nonparametric significance tests plus multiple-comparison corrections; (3) full numeric ablation tables for all input combinations and one-output vs two-output variants; (4) explicit documentation or re-runs demonstrating baseline/hyperparameter parity (shared embeddings, seed, optimizer); (5) attention visualizations, calibration analysis for o2 confidences, and targeted error analysis for embedded-source/multi-cue cases. These artifacts are essential for verifying claims and for the community to reproduce the work.

human_facing_meta_review.comments:
Summary:
The manuscript proposes a modular two-stage approach to event factuality on FactBank: (1) automated factor extraction (events, SIPs via PSen + attention-CNN, sources, cues) and (2) an attention-equipped neural factuality classifier that encodes shortest dependency paths with BiLSTM and auxiliary words with CNN, using a two-output design to separate Uu/Non-Uu and cue-driven modality/polarity. Reported results (Tables 3 and 4) show BiLSTM+CNN(Att) attains the highest micro- and macro-averaged F1 among compared baselines and improves several low-frequency classes; ablation claims highlight SIP_Path and auxiliary words as important inputs and attention as beneficial.

Strengths:
- Modular, linguistically-grounded pipeline that isolates factor extraction and classification and documents extraction metrics (Table 3).
- Architecture maps model components to linguistic signals (SDPs for syntactic relations, Aux Words for lexical markers) and uses attention to focus on salient tokens.
- Explicit focus on minority factuality labels with a two-output design to mitigate class imbalance; per-class F1s suggest improvements for CT-, PR+, PS+.
- PSen is a concrete engineering idea for SIP detection; attention-CNN on PSen is a reasonable, task-focused contribution.

Limitations:
- Attribution confound: the classifier operates on predicted SIP/source/cue outputs; no oracle-input experiments are reported, so it is unclear whether gains are due to classifier architecture or to pipeline extraction quality (Table 3 vs Table 4 dependency). (Major)
- Statistical reporting under-specified: p-values are reported from 5-fold CV/t-tests without per-fold numbers, effect sizes, or multiple-comparison corrections; two-sample t-test across n=5 may violate assumptions. (Major)
- Ablation and numerical reporting gaps: Figure 6 and single-output vs two-output comparisons lack full numeric per-class and per-fold tables, reducing reproducibility and preventing verification of per-input contributions. (Moderate)
- Baseline parity unclear: exact embedding initializations, optimizer settings, seeds and tuning procedures for baselines are not fully documented; differences could bias comparisons. (Moderate)

Open Questions:
1) Can the authors run the factuality classifier with gold SIP/cue/source inputs (and hybrid mixes) and report per-class/per-fold results to quantify sensitivity to extraction errors?  
2) Please provide per-fold numeric results (per-class P/R/F and micro/macro) for all systems and ablations so that paired tests, effect sizes, and multiple-comparison corrections can be computed and verified.  
3) What exact configurations were used for each baseline (embedding file and source, random seeds, parser versions, optimizer and learning-rate schedules, tuning budget)? If not identical, can baselines be re-run under matched settings?  
4) For multi-cue events, how often does the highest-confidence o2 heuristic pick the correct cue? Provide calibration analyses (reliability diagrams/ECE) for o2 and report alternative aggregation strategies.  
5) Provide attention visualizations and qualitative examples showing what tokens/positions attention focuses on and an error analysis for low Uu F1 on embedded sources.  
6) Report robustness to parser noise and to random seed variability (multiple runs) for main model variants.

Transparency:
Present: clear architecture descriptions, equations, diagrams, factor-extraction metrics (Table 3), classifier per-class and aggregate F1s (Table 4), plotted ablation (Figure 6), and some hyperparameters for proposed models.  
Missing: per-fold metric data underlying p-values (means ± SD), effect sizes, degrees of freedom, details about whether t-tests were paired, multiple-comparison corrections, full numeric ablation tables (per-class P/R/F per ablation, per-fold), exact baseline hyperparameters and embeddings, PSen construction code, random seeds, and model checkpoints. These missing artifacts impede reproduction of the statistical claims and independent causal attribution.

confidence_interval.rationale: I am moderately confident in the descriptive accuracy of the claims and identified methodological gaps because the manuscript includes tables and architecture descriptions supporting the points. However, lack of per-fold statistics, oracle-input experiments, and full ablation numeric data introduces substantial uncertainty about causal attribution and statistical robustness; hence a wide interval reflecting moderate-to-high epistemic uncertainty.
